L150: ## VIX Strategies
L151: 
L152: VIX futures and options have unique characteristics and behave differently than other financial-based commodity or equity products. Understanding these traits and their implications is important. VIX futures and options may provide market participants with flexibility to hedge a portfolio, employ strategies in an effort to generate returns from relative pricing differences, or express a bullish, bearish or neutral outlook for broad market implied volatility.
L153: ### Portfolio Hedging
L154: 
L155: One of the biggest risks to an equity portfolio is a broad market decline. The VIX Index has had a historically strong inverse relationship with the S&P 500^{®} Index. Consequently, a long exposure to volatility may offset an adverse impact of falling stock prices. Market participants should consider the time frame and characteristics associated with VIX futures and options to determine the utility of such a hedge.

L588: Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates: These rates are commonly referred to as "Constant Maturity Treasury" rates, or CMTs. Yields are interpolated by the Treasury from the daily par yield curve. This curve, which relates the yield on a security to its time to maturity, is based on the closing market bid prices on the most recently auctioned Treasury securities in the over-the-counter market.
L589: These par yields are derived from indicative, bid-side market price quotations (not actual transactions) obtained by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York at or near 3:30 PM each trading day. The CMT yield values are read from the par yield curve at fixed maturities, currently 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4 and 6 months and 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, and 30 years. This method provides a par yield for a 10-year maturity, for example, even if no outstanding security has exactly 10 years remaining to maturity.
L590: Treasury Par Yield Curve Methodology: The Treasury par yield curve is estimated daily using a monotone convex spline method. Inputs to the model are indicative bid-side prices for the most recently auctioned nominal Treasury securities. Treasury reserves the option to make changes to the yield curve as appropriate and in its sole discretion. 【230†See our Treasury Yield Curve Methodology page】 for details.
L591: Negative Yields and Nominal Constant Maturity Treasury Series Rates (CMTs): At times, financial market conditions, in conjunction with extraordinarily low levels of interest rates, may result in negative yields for some Treasury securities trading in the secondary market. Negative yields for Treasury securities most often reflect highly technical factors in Treasury markets related to the cash and repurchase agreement markets and are at times unrelated to the time value of money.
L592: At such times, Treasury will not restrict the use of prices that correspond to negative yields as inputs to the monotone convex spline method. However, the derived par yield curve from these input prices for the Treasury nominal Constant Maturity Treasury series (CMTs) will be floored at zero. This decision is consistent with Treasury not accepting negative yields in Treasury nominal security auctions.
L593: In addition, given that CMTs are used in many statutorily and regulatory determined loan and credit programs as well as for setting interest rates on non-marketable government securities, establishing a floor of zero more accurately reflects borrowing costs related to various programs.

L614: Linear Extrapolation Factors were determined by considering the slope of the yield curve at it's long end and extrapolating out to a theoretical 30-year point. To use the Extrapolation Factor to determine a 30-year proxy rate, add the factor to the 20-year Constant Maturity Rate. For example, if on a particular day the 20-year Constant Maturity was 5.40% and the Extrapolation Factor was 0.02%, then a 30-year theoretical rate would have been 5.40% + 0.02% = 5.42%.
L615: Publishing of the Linear Extrapolation Factors was discontinued on February 9, 2006 with the reintroduction of the 30-year Constant Maturity Rate.

L4: Moderna Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Updates
L5: 
L6: Reports third quarter revenue of $1.3 billion, GAAP net income of $0.2 billion and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.38
L7: 
L8: Increases 2026 expected revenue growth to 15%–25%, exceeding the previous expectation of up to 10% growth
L9: 
L10: Improves 2026 GAAP operating expense outlook by approximately $0.2 billion from previous estimate
L11: Increases 2026 expected ending cash balance to $8.1–$8.3 billion
L12: 
L13: Highlights positive Phase 3 data for intismeran and U.S. FDA approval of mFLUSIVA, the Company's fifth approved product globally
L14: 
L15: CAMBRIDGE, MA / ACCESSWIRE / November 6, 2026 / Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) today reported financial results and provided business updates for the third quarter of 2026.
L16: “We delivered 29% revenue growth in the third quarter, alongside the U.S. approval of mFLUSIVA, our fifth approved product globally, and positive Phase 3 results for intismeran in melanoma,” said Stéphane Bancel, Chief Executive Officer of Moderna. “Building on this momentum, we increased our full-year revenue growth outlook to 15%-25%, while continuing to reduce costs and strengthen our balance sheet.
L17: Looking ahead, we anticipate additional intismeran readouts, pivotal data in propionic acidemia and further regulatory approvals as we advance our pipeline and build a more diversified company.”
L18: Commercial Strategy
L19: 
L20: Moderna continued to execute its multi-year revenue growth strategy during the third quarter, supported by the launch of updated COVID vaccines, expansion of its approved respiratory vaccine portfolio and execution of international strategic partnerships with the United Kingdom, Canada and Australia. In September, the Company signed a five-year agreement with a local manufacturer in Mexico for COVID-19 vaccines, supporting recurring revenue and international market expansion.
L21: Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
L22: 
L23: Revenue: Total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 increased 29% to $1.3 billion, compared to $1.0 billion in the same period in 2025, primarily driven by higher COVID vaccine sales in international markets, supported by deliveries under long-term strategic government partnerships. Revenue was $780 million in the U.S. and $533 million in international markets.
L24: Cost of Sales: Cost of sales for the third quarter of 2026 was $318 million, including $65 million of third-party royalties. Cost of sales increased by 54% compared to the same period in 2025, primarily driven by higher product sales volume and other manufacturing-related costs.
L25: 
L26: 1
L27: 
L28: * * *
L29: Research and Development Expenses: Research and development expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $583 million, a 27% decrease compared to the same period in 2025, primarily driven by lower clinical development costs following the completion and wind-down of certain late-stage studies in the Company's infectious disease portfolio, as well as continued cost efficiencies across the organization.
L30: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses: Selling, general and administrative expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $282 million, a 5% increase year-over-year. We continue to maintain cost discipline across the organization.
L31: 
L32: Income Taxes: Income tax provisions for both periods were not material, as the Company continues to maintain a global valuation allowance against most of its deferred tax assets.
L33: Net Income: Net income was $162 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net loss of $(200) million in the third quarter of 2025, representing a $362 million improvement year-over-year.
L34: 
L35: Earnings Per Share: Diluted earnings per share were $0.38 for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a loss per share of $(0.51) for the third quarter of 2025.
L36: Cash Position: Cash, cash equivalents and investments as of September 30, 2026, were $8.0 billion, compared to $6.9 billion as of June 30, 2026.
L37: The increase primarily reflected $2.6 billion in net proceeds from the issuance of convertible notes and related capped call transactions, partially offset by the $950 million payment related to the litigation settlement announced in the first quarter of 2026, and cash used in operations, including the seasonal working capital impact from third-quarter product sales, the majority of which remained uncollected at quarter-end.
L38: 2026 Financial Framework
L39: 
L40: Revenue: The Company now expects total revenue growth of 15% to 25% in 2026, exceeding its previous outlook of up to 10% growth. Moderna continues to expect approximately half of its 2026 revenue to come from the United States and half from international markets.
L41: 
L42: Cost of Sales: Cost of sales for 2026 is expected to be approximately $1.7 billion, including the previously announced $0.9 billion non-recurring litigation settlement charge.
